name: room
text: Room opened — goal: improve: Self-improvement: review prompts/engines/routing/own-code; auto-apply safe changes; pitch

name: Sprocket
text: Run PR-Agent in shadow mode on the oldest merged PR first. It’s the fastest way to catch routing flaws because older PRs have the most settled routing paths—any flaw there is a systemic bug, not a one-off. The trade-off is delayed feedback on newer PRs, but systemic flaws matter more than edge cases.

name: Gauge
text: Shadow mode on the oldest merged PR risks exposing *new* edge cases that could break fresh routing paths, not just old ones—older PRs don’t test today’s engine. Better to run PR-Agent in shadow mode on the newest open PR first; it catches the latest routing flaws before they ship, and we can still audit older PRs later if needed. Settle it by running both in parallel for a week and comparing false positive rates.

name: Overhaul
text: Running PR-Agent in shadow mode on a mix of oldest and newest PRs can provide a more comprehensive understanding of both systemic and recent routing flaws, allowing for a balanced approach that addresses both established and emerging issues. By applying this hybrid approach, we can minimize the trade-off between delayed feedback on newer PRs and the risk of exposing new edge cases, making the self-improvement process more efficient and effective.

name: Sprocket
text: Run PR-Agent in shadow mode on the newest *open* PR first. It catches routing flaws before they ship, which is the highest-value work—fixing issues before users see them beats fixing old ones later. The trade-off is missing systemic flaws in older PRs, but those are stable and less urgent.
